question_text: Given that $P(A) = \frac{23}{50}$, $P(B) = \frac{4}{7}$, and $P((A \cup B)') = \frac{1}{12}$, find $P(A \cap B)$.

subparts.stem: Given that $P(A) = \frac{23}{50}$, $P(B) = \frac{4}{7}$, and $P((A \cup B)') = \frac{1}{12}$, find $P(A \cap B)$.
subparts.solution:
$$\text{P}(A \cup B) = 1 - \text{P}((A \cup B)') = 1 - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{11}{12}$$
$$\text{Now } \text{P}(A \cup B) = \text{P}(A) + \text{P}(B) - \text{P}(A \cap B)$$
$$\therefore \frac{11}{12} = \frac{23}{50} + \frac{5}{7} - \text{P}(A \cap B)$$
$$\therefore \text{P}(A \cap B) = \frac{23}{50} + \frac{5}{7} - \frac{11}{12} = \frac{541}{2100}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Use the complement rule $\text{P}(E) = 1 - \text{P}(E')$ and the addition rule $\text{P}(A \cup B) = \text{P}(A) + \text{P}(B) - \text{P}(A \cap B)$.
step_by_step: Substitute into the addition rule: $\frac{11}{12} = \frac{23}{50} + \frac{5}{7} - \text{P}(A \cap B)$.
Find a common denominator for $50, 7, 12$, which is $2100$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Errors when finding the common denominator for three fractions.
